section_summary: This section follows disputes over Japan’s postwar petroleum distribution system, especially Standard-Vacuum’s effort to regain access to its properties and market. It includes State Department correspondence, occupation authorities’ explanations of the temporary Petroleum Distribution Kodan, and statistics for 1945–46. The final pages introduce a proposed government commission to develop Japan’s domestic oil resources; its supporting study continues beyond page 68.

subfiles.title: Telegram on contract copy held in Legation safe
subfiles.about: Clarifies that a photostatic contract copy is in the Legation safe.
subfiles.summary: Reports receipt of the contract copy on October 31 and corrects a misunderstanding.

subfiles.title: Enclosure charge slip
subfiles.about: Records an enclosure charge.
subfiles.summary: Partly illegible administrative charge slip.

subfiles.title: Union Oil protest concerning petroleum distribution monopoly
subfiles.about: Protests a proposed government-controlled petroleum distribution monopoly in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Union Oil argues that the proposal could obstruct competitive trade and its longstanding Japanese business.

subfiles.title: Reply to Ole Berg Jr. on proposed distribution corporation
subfiles.about: Explains the proposed temporary Japanese government petroleum distribution corporation.
subfiles.summary: The corporation would lease predecessor companies’ facilities, handle domestic distribution, and dissolve when private trade becomes feasible.

subfiles.title: Questions to SCAP on Japanese oil distribution corporation
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asks whether the corporation replaces earlier bodies, how long it will operate, and what happens to their facilities.
subfiles.summary: Requests clarification of the new distribution corporation’s scope, duration, and leased facilities.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on government oil distribution corporation
subfiles.about: Answers State’s questions on the proposed corporation.
subfiles.summary: Says it will replace PDCC and PDC, operate temporarily, and lease their facilities.

subfiles.title: Notes on Socony and Japanese petroleum refining
subfiles.about: Discusses Socony’s concerns about Japanese refinery capacity and reparations.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten notes question whether Japanese refining costs and capacity justify preserving refineries, and refer to Socony’s recommendations.

subfiles.title: Socony memorandum on oil refineries in Japan
subfiles.about: Summarizes a conversation about Socony’s preferred future in Japanese petroleum trade.
subfiles.summary: Socony prefers importing refined products while protecting its longstanding market and questions the economics of imported-crude refining.

subfiles.title: Digest of Standard-Vacuum memorandum to P. P. Claxton
subfiles.about: Summarizes Standard-Vacuum’s concerns about Japan’s refining capacity, properties, and future trade.
subfiles.summary: Standard-Vacuum seeks drastic refinery reparations or a stake in Japanese refineries. It also asks to inspect and rehabilitate its property and correspond with its occupation advisers.

subfiles.title: Handwritten routing note
subfiles.about: Requests follow-up on a point in the attached papers.
subfiles.summary: Brief, largely illegible handwritten note.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum memorandum to P. P. Claxton
subfiles.about: Argues that retaining Japanese refining capacity threatens Standard-Vacuum’s market and investment.
subfiles.summary: Reviews its prewar trade and investment, Japanese consumption forecasts, and proposed refinery capacity. If substantial refining capacity remains after reparations, it seeks U.S. help acquiring an interest in modern Japanese refineries.

subfiles.title: Exhibit A: Standard-Vacuum memorandum on Japan
subfiles.about: Explains how Japanese refining and distribution plans could exclude imported refined products.
subfiles.summary: Describes Standard-Vacuum’s prewar facilities and fears that Japanese refineries will absorb the market. It asks to protect its properties and permit correspondence with its Petroleum Advisory Group representative.

subfiles.title: Exhibit B: Memorandum to Major General Frank R. McCoy
subfiles.about: Assesses refinery capacity and options for Standard-Vacuum’s postwar business.
subfiles.summary: Estimates that surviving Japanese refineries could meet projected consumption and block product imports. Standard-Vacuum asks for reparations policy information and, if capacity remains, an opportunity to acquire existing refining facilities.

subfiles.title: Despatch on petroleum for British Commonwealth occupation forces
subfiles.about: Forwards an Australian petroleum supply invitation for forces in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a letter of possible interest to agencies supplying Japan.

subfiles.title: Bulk supply of petroleum products for B.C.O.F., Japan
subfiles.from: J. Raw, Australian Department of Supply and Shipping
subfiles.about: Invites interest in contracts to supply petroleum products to Kure from sterling sources.
subfiles.summary: Sets eligibility, shipment, and response requirements for prospective tenderers.

subfiles.title: Routing note for Standard-Vacuum letter
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Routes correspondence for appropriate action.
subfiles.summary: Administrative direction to take appropriate action.

subfiles.title: Parker letter on repossession and petroleum distribution
subfiles.about: Seeks access to Standard-Vacuum’s Japanese properties and participation in petroleum distribution.
subfiles.summary: Parker argues that continued Japanese use of the firm’s property harms its investment and risks nationalization. He proposes authorizing company advisers in Tokyo to protect facilities and participate in distribution.

subfiles.title: Interim acknowledgment of Parker’s proposals
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Parker’s proposals concerning Standard-Vacuum’s Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Promises departmental study and a later substantive reply.

subfiles.title: Martin reply on the Petroleum Distribution Kodan
subfiles.about: Conveys SCAP’s response on Kodan, rentals, compensation, and company representation.
subfiles.summary: Explains that Kodan leases property temporarily and must pay reasonable rentals. Wartime losses remain potential claims; foreign representatives may return when conditions permit.

subfiles.title: Thorp interim reply on Parker’s March letter
subfiles.about: Reports that SCAP has been asked to comment on Parker’s objections.
subfiles.summary: States that the corporation is temporary, provides rentals, and awaits a fuller Tokyo response.

subfiles.title: State Department request for SCAP views on foreign oil property
subfiles.about: Requests comment on American and British concerns about the distribution monopoly and foreign-owned property.
subfiles.summary: Relays Standard-Vacuum’s objections and British concerns over leases. It asks SCAP about property protection, compensation, and possible company representatives.

subfiles.title: Petroleum statistics on Japan for 1945 and 1946
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits seven sets of Japanese petroleum statistics.
subfiles.summary: Lists enclosed production, drilling, refining, marketing, import, stock, and price tables.

subfiles.title: Crude oil production statistics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates Japanese crude oil production by prefecture for 1945 and 1946.
subfiles.summary: Reports production in Hokkaido, Akita, Niigata, Yamagata, and Shizuoka.

subfiles.title: Drilling statistics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates exploratory and exploitation wells for 1945 and 1946.
subfiles.summary: Counts oil producers, gas producers, and abandonments.

subfiles.title: Refining statistics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates refinery inputs and outputs for 1945 and 1946.
subfiles.summary: Breaks out domestic and foreign crude inputs and principal refined products.

subfiles.title: Petroleum marketing statistics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates Japanese petroleum sales by product for 1945 and 1946.
subfiles.summary: Provides sales volumes for fuels, lubricants, wax, and asphalt.

subfiles.title: Petroleum import statistics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates petroleum product imports for 1945 and 1946.
subfiles.summary: Shows U.S. sources and a sharp rise in 1946 imports.

subfiles.title: Petroleum stock statistics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates crude and product stocks for 1945 and 1946.
subfiles.summary: Lists inventories of fuels, lubricants, wax, and asphalt.

subfiles.title: Petroleum price statistics
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates Japanese petroleum prices in yen.
subfiles.summary: Lists crude and product prices and identifies the transactions used for crude prices.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Tokyo petroleum statistics
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of the Tokyo petroleum statistics despatch.
subfiles.summary: Transmits despatch 981 on Japan’s 1945–46 petroleum statistics.

subfiles.title: SCAP response concerning Petroleum Distribution Kodan
subfiles.about: Explains Kodan’s temporary role, leases, compensation rules, and foreign firms’ return.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says Kodan must maintain leased property and pay equitable compensation. It outlines possible claims for wartime losses, acknowledges a risk of later nationalization, and favors restoring commercial operations when conditions allow.

subfiles.title: Conversation on petroleum industry problems in Japan
subfiles.about: Records discussion of quotas, refinery estimates, property inspection, and company advisers.
subfiles.summary: Participants discuss whether Petroleum Advisory Group members could act for their companies and whether a restitution mission could adequately inspect properties.

subfiles.title: Parker’s renewed protest against the Kodan
subfiles.about: Challenges continued exclusion of Standard-Vacuum and seeks stronger safeguards.
subfiles.summary: Parker fears Kodan may become permanent and asks for foreign-company re-entry, retroactive rent, and protection against depreciation of yen payments.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum on Parker’s May letter
subfiles.about: Reviews the handling of Parker’s renewed protest.
subfiles.summary: Notes that SCAP has addressed its main points and a company representative may inspect property through a restitution mission.

subfiles.title: Copy of Martin reply on the Petroleum Distribution Kodan
subfiles.about: Restates SCAP’s position on temporary Kodan operations and foreign property.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the substantive reply appearing on pages 27–28, covering leases, compensation, possible claims, and eventual company representation.

subfiles.title: Thorp acknowledgment of Parker’s May letter
subfiles.about: Acknowledges renewed objections to Kodan’s use of Standard-Vacuum property.
subfiles.summary: Promises to seek Tokyo’s comments and send a further reply.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Japanese oil tankage as reparations
subfiles.about: Considers removing surplus Japanese oil tanks for countries needing replacement storage.
subfiles.summary: deBlank proposes interim removal of Japanese tankage; Martin suggests interagency consultation before seeking action.

subfiles.title: Parker proposals for restoring private petroleum trade
subfiles.about: Proposes deadlines for ending Kodan and restoring commercial importation and distribution.
subfiles.summary: Parker asks that Kodan and Josco end by March 1948, foreign facilities be returned, and foreign firms regain access to distribution infrastructure.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Parker’s July letter to Tokyo
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards Parker’s letter for General Headquarters’ consideration.
subfiles.summary: Requests whatever action General Headquarters considers appropriate.

subfiles.title: Proposed Petroleum Resources Development Commission Bill
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a preliminary SCAP staff study on proposed Japanese oil legislation.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the enclosed draft lacks final staff and chief-of-staff approval.

subfiles.title: Draft memorandum recommending a Petroleum Resources Development Commission
subfiles.from: Hubert G. Schenck, Natural Resources Section
subfiles.about: Recommends a government commission to replace Imperial Oil Company and maintain domestic crude production.
subfiles.summary: The study argues that integrated exploration and production are essential, while Imperial Oil’s mixed ownership and near-monopoly are undesirable. It recommends no objection to a commission bill if specified safeguards are retained.

subfiles.title: Proposed Petroleum Resources Development Commission Bill: provisions
subfiles.from: Leo W. Stach, Natural Resources Section
subfiles.about: Outlines the proposed commission’s powers, funding, limits, and review.
subfiles.summary: The commission would take over Imperial Oil’s production assets, explore for reserves, assist independents, and undergo Diet review after four years. Its leases and operations would be restricted to oil exploration and production.

subfiles.title: Situation of the petroleum producing industry in Japan
subfiles.about: Surveys Imperial Oil’s history, ownership, production decline, exploration needs, and structural problems.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces Imperial Oil’s wartime mergers, shareholders, and falling output. It argues that intensive, integrated exploration is needed to replace depleted reserves and describes promising new fields. It also identifies problems in the company’s government-backed monopoly. The memorandum continues after page 68.
